title: How She Turned One Vending Location Into $25K a Month
excerpt: Shan relocated to Seattle for her husband's job, started vending to help fund a home remodel, and turned one micro market into $22-25K a month.
quote: This one space changed everything for my husband and I.
body:
## Background

Shan relocated from the Bay Area to Seattle for her husband's new job. Her own role wasn't fully remote, leaving her under-employed and, in her words, bored. They had just bought a home that needed a remodel, so they were paying Seattle rent and a Seattle mortgage at the same time. Mike walked her through how to start a business from the ground up.

> We were paying Seattle rent and a Seattle mortgage, which is a really fun thing to do — like, talk about just catching money on fire.

## The Challenge

Shan had zero business background going in — she didn't even know what an LLC was. The first six months were overwhelming: inventory took over the living room and dining room of their 800-square-foot home, and within 48 hours of opening she got an email warning that the machine had already sold out and asking if she was coming back.

> I had no business background. I had no business being in this business. I never knew what an LLC was. I didn't know what I was doing.

## The Turning Point

Mike walked her through the fundamentals of starting a business before she had any idea the location would turn out to be special. She invested $10,000 to $12,000 in a micro market setup, which paid itself off quickly once the location took off.

> I was really lucky to have Mike kind of walk me through a bunch of different areas and different steps about what does it really look like, how do you start your own business from the ground up.

## Where They Are Now

A year and a half in, Shan runs four locations. Her first — a micro market inside a mixed-use Seattle high-rise with condos, apartments, and a long-term hotel — averages $22,000 to $25,000 a month in sales. Smartwater alone brings in about $6,000 a month, and a six-pack of Charmin toilet paper sells for $16.99 at roughly 50 percent margin. She hired a stocker off Craigslist and moved into warehouse space with receiving, which finally made the business feel passive.

> There is nothing passive when you get started. Now is passive.
